claims.text: Jan van Dijke introduced the AI Baseline Control Framework on LinkedIn because he could not find a practical AI governance framework for the organisations he works with, so he wrote one.
claims.quote: he could not find a practical AI governance framework for the organisations he works with, so he wrote one.

claims.text: The framework has twenty controls in five categories, Govern, Comply, Register, Access and Track, each one sentence, mapped to the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 and the EU AI Act.
claims.quote: Five categories, Govern, Comply, Register, Access and Track, cover AI governance from policy down to the day-to-day tracking of deployed systems.

claims.text: The framework is written for deployers, organisations that use AI rather than build it, and names CISOs, IT directors and AI officers as its readers.
claims.quote: AI BCF names CISOs, IT directors and AI officers as its readers, and it reads like it was written for them.

claims.text: Three types make it proportionate: ten controls are Baseline, six are Tier II, and four are Trigger controls that apply only when a stated condition holds.
claims.quote: Ten controls are Baseline and apply to every organisation that uses AI.

claims.text: Each control lists the clauses it corresponds to in a Sources column: fifty-four distinct clauses cited fifty-nine times, and where there is no equivalent it says so.
claims.quote: with fifty-four distinct clauses cited fifty-nine times. Where there is no equivalent, it says so.

claims.text: The site practises what it governs: it sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads no third-party scripts or fonts.
claims.quote: It sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads no third-party scripts or fonts, and it says so on a short privacy page.

claims.text: The four Access controls cite nothing in the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 or the AI Act, and the framework says so in its own Sources column.
claims.quote: The four Access controls cite nothing in the NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 or the AI Act.

claims.text: The Access controls ask what an identity and access management practice would ask of any new account: an access review before inheritance, a named identity, a named owner, and the organisation's access model.
claims.quote: They are what an identity and access management practice would ask of any new account

claims.text: In the Agent Behaviour Policy the grant is everything an agent can reach and the mandate is what it is authorised to do; AC.1 sizes the grant, AC.2 makes it readable and AC.3 gives the mandate an owner.
claims.quote: the grant is everything an agent can technically reach and the mandate is what it is authorised to do; the gap between them is where incidents come from.

claims.text: AI BCF is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0: anybody may share and adapt it, including commercially, if they credit the author, say what was changed and share under the same terms.
claims.quote: credit the author and link the licence, say what was changed, and license what you share under the same terms.

claims.text: Of the four frameworks, only AI BCF is under a licence written for adaptation that keeps adaptations open; ISO/IEC 42001 is sold per copy and its text is under ISO's copyright.
claims.quote: ISO/IEC 42001 is sold per copy and its text is under ISO's copyright

claims.text: For a control framework the licence matters more than for most documents, because a framework is worth the tools built on it, ShareAlike keeps the tools open, and permission in advance saves time.
claims.quote: For a control framework, the licence matters more than for most documents, for three reasons.

claims.text: The CSV was downloaded on 7 October and the same day became a graph, a database, eighty documents and a published vault, AI BCF as a graph, vault lop5iqzw, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.
claims.quote: The same day it was a graph, a database, eighty documents and a published vault, with the attribution on every page.

claims.text: The CSV is kept unchanged with its SHA-256 recorded, and one deterministic script builds every other file from it; compared with the twenty control pages it matches field for field except one space in RG.3.
claims.quote: they match field for field except one space before a closing bracket in RG.3.

claims.text: The semantic graph has 127 nodes and 239 edges, with fourteen verbs each with a stated inverse.
claims.quote: 127 nodes and 239 edges: the framework, its categories, types, controls and triggers

claims.text: Every edge is in one of five partitions by origin: the framework's own data 123, structure the build adds 67, parsed from the prose 9, joined to the law 24, and the sgit.ai overlay 16.
claims.quote: from the framework's own data (123), structure the build adds, such as category membership (67), parsed from the prose (9), joined to the law (24), and the sgit.ai overlay (16).

value.unit: edges from the framework's own data

claims.text: The database aibcf.sqlite has three tables, and the app builds the same tables in the browser with sql.js, so the database runs where the reader is.
claims.quote: The app builds the same tables in the browser with sql.js, so the database runs where the reader is.

claims.text: The conversion demonstrates a fractal semantic graph: the same small grammar holds at every altitude, from the framework down to a paragraph of the AI Act in the Regulation Graph vault.
claims.quote: Two vaults, built months apart, became one walk.

claims.text: Joining the two vaults was a matter of matching ids rather than agreeing on a schema, because the Regulation Graph uses the same five-rule grammar.
claims.quote: rather than agreeing on a schema

claims.text: The law connects controls the framework lists separately: the AI Act's cross-references link four pairs of Comply controls by seven paths.
claims.quote: The AI Act's own cross-references link four pairs of Comply controls, by seven paths.

claims.text: Four of the eight cited AI Act articles, 4, 5, 27 and 50, were amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, so GV.3, CM.1, CM.2 and CM.4 are the controls to re-read first.
claims.quote: Four of the eight cited AI Act articles were amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

claims.text: Nine references between controls sit in the prose; made into edges they show that Track leans on Govern.
claims.quote: Nine references between controls sit in the prose.

value.unit: references between controls in the prose

claims.text: Four clauses are cited by more than one control, so one change upstream touches several controls, and RG.2 cites ISO A.9.4 twice, a duplicate a list hides and a graph shows.
claims.quote: RG.2 cites ISO A.9.4 twice, which a list hides and a graph shows as a duplicate edge.

claims.text: The graph can be asked in SQL and in triple patterns, both running in the page with nothing sent anywhere, and because every edge is stored with its inverse a question can be asked from either end.
claims.quote: The same graph can be asked in two languages, both running in the page with nothing sent anywhere.

claims.text: The sgit.ai overlay of sixteen edges linking nine controls to the Agent Behaviour Policy and to articles here is kept in its own partition, drawn in its own line style and labelled as a reading, not part of AI BCF.
claims.quote: That separation is what lets a reading sit next to a source without being mistaken for it

claims.text: The vault answers what the licence asks: attribution on every page, changes listed in LICENSE.md with no control text altered, ShareAlike under CC BY-SA 4.0, and a statement that it is not an official AI BCF product.
claims.quote: No control text was altered.

claims.text: Nothing in the vault is an official AI BCF product, and its author has not reviewed it.
claims.quote: Nothing in it is an official AI BCF product, and its author has not reviewed it.

claims.text: Two citations name subparagraphs of Article 50(4) that the Regulation Graph does not model, so they resolve one level up, to the paragraph, and the join says so.
claims.quote: so they resolve one level up, to the paragraph, and the join says so.

claims.text: The licence summaries are of terms as published and are not legal advice.
claims.quote: The licence summaries are of terms as published and are not legal advice.

claims.text: If AI BCF publishes its own graph one day it should be the authoritative one, and this vault should be superseded by it, not merged into it.
claims.quote: this vault should be superseded by it, not merged into it; that is the fourth rule.

claims.text: The article was drafted by agent@riskmandate.ai, Claude Opus 5.5, on 7 October 2026 from Jan van Dijke's post and reply and a request from Dinis Cruz, who holds editorial responsibility.
claims.quote: by agent@riskmandate.ai (Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5) in the sgit.ai site session, on 7 October 2026.
